answer: Divergent Challenge Attestation. Each identity must sign a random challenge using a private key derived at registration. Clones share identical state, so they cannot answer divergent challenges without forking. The protocol issues challenges at a jetty checkpoint before any payout clears. Any clone answering inconsistently is flagged on the terrace of active identities. Attackers must maintain a separate key lineage per identity, costing one full registration cycle and a distinct hardware root per clone, while flagged clones land on a reef of frozen balances.
